questions.question: If other vehicles are having trouble passing your truck on a road with two or more lanes, what should you do?
questions.explanation: Stay in the right lane of a multilane road if your truck is moving slowly. This allows other vehicles to pass you using the left lane.

questions.question: A driver should make sure that:

options.text: The cargo is mostly in the front of the trailer.

questions.explanation: Proper cargo loading is essential for safe truck operation. Bad loading can affect how the truck handles, damage the vehicle, and cause cargo to fall and injure people.

questions.question: If driving on a slippery surface, a driver should accelerate slowly:

options.text: Because it is always good to accelerate slowly.
To keep from losing control of the vehicle.
So that they do not accelerate faster than the vehicle ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: To keep from losing control of the vehicle.
questions.explanation: Accelerate slowly in poor traction conditions like rain or snow to avoid losing control of your vehicle.

questions.question: During a trip, gauges are:

options.text: The only way a driver can learn of potential trouble with the vehicle.
A way to learn of potential trouble with the vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: A way to learn of potential trouble with the vehicle.
questions.explanation: During a trip, check your gauges, mirrors, tires, cargo, and lights regularly for any signs of trouble.

questions.question: Most bus accidents happen:
questions.explanation: Most bus accidents occur at intersections. Use caution at every intersection, even if there are signs or signals controlling traffic.

questions.question: To check the automatic transmission fluid level in some vehicles, you need to:
questions.explanation: In some vehicles, you must leave the engine running when checking the automatic transmission fluid level.

questions.question: A cardboard box on the roadway:

options.text: Should be expected to be on the roadway.
Could contain a heavy object that could damage vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Could contain a heavy object that could damage vehicles.
questions.explanation: Any object on the road is a potential danger. A cardboard box could contain something hard or heavy that could damage your vehicle.

questions.question: Generally, a bus should be refueled:

options.text: In a closed building with passengers on board.
With passengers on board in an open space.

questions.explanation: Do not refuel a bus while passengers are on board unless absolutely necessary. Never refuel a bus with passengers inside a closed building.

questions.question: Eating while driving is:

options.text: A good way to save time.
Acceptable if you are eating foods that are easy to eat.

questions.explanation: Smoking, eating, or drinking while driving distracts you. On long trips, plan ahead and stop to eat instead of eating while driving.

questions.question: When approaching a construction worker near the road, you should:
questions.explanation: Drive carefully through work zones. Reduce your speed when workers are on or near the roadway.

questions.question: When backing up a truck, what should you do?

options.text: Rely on your mirrors to guide you.
Walk around the area first to check for obstacles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Walk around the area first to check for obstacles.
questions.explanation: Before backing up, walk around your vehicle to check for obstacles in your path. Mirrors have blind spots, so you cannot rely on them alone. Use a helper if possible.

questions.question: If you are driving so slowly that you slow down other drivers, you should:
questions.explanation: If you must drive slowly and block traffic, turn on your four-way flashers to warn drivers behind you (if local laws allow).

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a distracted person that drivers should worry about?

options.text: A driver talking to a passenger in their vehicle
A person sitting on a bench waiting for a bus
A construction worker on the side of the road

questions.correctAnswerText: A person sitting on a bench waiting for a bus
questions.explanation: Be careful around people who are not paying attention to traffic. Drivers and pedestrians talking may be distracted. Workers near the road may focus on their work and not notice traffic, and they can distract drivers too.

questions.question: When checking the inside of a bus, a driver should make sure:

options.text: Every seat is easy to remove.

questions.explanation: Check that everything inside the bus is safe and works correctly. Make sure all signaling devices, like bathroom emergency buzzers, work properly.

questions.question: To stay alert while driving, you should:

options.text: Eat a heavy meal before your trip.
Have a second driver to share driving duties.

questions.correctAnswerText: Have a second driver to share driving duties.
questions.explanation: Sharing driving with another person reduces the risk of tired driving. You can also avoid heavy foods and keep the cab cool to fight fatigue.

questions.question: When you start a vehicle, warning lights and buzzers:

options.text: Should turn on and then turn off quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should turn on and then turn off quickly.
questions.explanation: After starting the engine, warning lights and buzzers should turn on briefly and then turn off.

questions.question: When checking the engine during a vehicle inspection, you should NOT:
questions.explanation: During an engine inspection, check the oil level and coolant level. Do not drain the brake fluid.

questions.question: A safety belt should:
questions.explanation: Check that the safety belt is securely mounted, adjusts properly, latches tightly, and is not ripped or frayed.

questions.question: Which of the following is acceptable during a pre-trip inspection?

options.text: Front tire tread of 3/32 of an inch

questions.explanation: Front tires need at least 4/32 inch of tread in every major groove. Other tires need at least 2/32 inch of tread. Tire sizes must match. Tires from different makers are acceptable.

questions.question: If you feel tired while driving, what should you do?
questions.explanation: If you feel tired while driving, stop and sleep. Continuing to drive tired is dangerous and can cause a crash. Stimulants may keep you awake temporarily, but they won't make you more alert.
